sources.entry: CUPS - The Common Unix Print System uses Internet Printing Protocol (IPP) to support printing to local and network printers. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 C

summary.one_liner: CUPS is the OpenPrinting Common Unix Print System, a standards-based (IPP) printing server and toolkit for Linux and other Unix-like systems.
summary.what_it_does: CUPS prints to AirPrint and IPP Everywhere printers, to network and USB printers via Printer Applications, and to legacy printers using PPD-based drivers. It provides the System V "lp" and Berkeley "lpr" command-line interfaces, plus the lpadmin and lpinfo tools for managing queues and listing drivers and devices. It includes a configurable web administration interface for managing printers, classes, and jobs. It also offers a C API, along with common print filters, drivers, and backends. The README notes that the cups-filters project provides additional filters and drivers.
use_cases: set up a network printer on Linux
print documents from the command line
manage print queues and jobs through a web interface
print to AirPrint or IPP Everywhere printers
label printing with Zebra or Dymo printers
notable: Supports AirPrint and IPP Everywhere driverless printing
Provides both System V lp and Berkeley lpr command-line interfaces
Includes sample PPD drivers for many legacy printers, including Dymo, Epson, HP, OKIDATA and Zebra
caveats: The README describes this as the 2.5b1 pre-release branch tracking a future 2.5.x feature release; the 2.4.x branch is the stable line
Additional filters and drivers come from the separate cups-filters project
Administration requires a password for root or a member of the sys, system, root, admin, or lpadmin group
summary.license: Apache License 2.0 with an exception allowing linking against GPL2-only software (metadata lists GPL-2.0; README states Apache 2.0)
